name: Marenje
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Alfazema, Cantauile, Rijone & Kroger 2006, Algumas notas gramaticais sobre a lingua Imarenje (SIL Mozambique, 23 pp. grammar sketch); also SIL 2009/2013 grammar sketches
earlier_scan.note: Makhuwa-group Bantu; SIL grammar sketch plausibly states penultimate stress/length but former host lidemo.net is dead and no online copy found.

sources.citation: SIL. 2013. Notas gramaticais sobre Emakhuwa-Imeetto, 2nd edn. Monografias Linguísticas Moçambicanas 6. Nampula: SIL Moçambique. 44 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Listed by Glottolog under mare1260; the opened 2009 edition is silent on stress and describes Makhuwa-Meetto (mgh), so this is needed only to confirm the 2nd edition adds nothing and to correct the Glottolog attribution.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mare1260 and reference pages 94422, 577247, 317873, 18147, 108488, 129180, 33721; lidemo.net 'Marenje [vmr]' page (the Internet Archive 2013-10-17); the Internet Archive's index index of lidemo.net (687 URLs)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. The CDX index shows vmr_p000631/vmr_v000631 (Alfazema et al. 2006) as the only Marenje document SIL Mozambique ever hosted; no Emarenje vocabulary or phonology exists there. Searches of archive.org, Google Books API, OpenAlex, CrossRef returned nothing further for Imarenje/Marenje (Google Books has only a no-preview record of Alfazema et al. 2006). Bing/DDG/Mojeek/Brave/Scholar/HathiTrust/Ethnologue/sil.

sources.citation: Alfazema, J. P. M., J. S. Cantauíle, M. H. J. Rijone & H. Kröger. 2006. Algumas notas gramaticais sobre Imarenje. Monografias Linguísticas Moçambicanas 3. Nampula: SIL Moçambique. 1st electronic edn 2010, 40 pp. (A5 'v' file) + booklet-imposed 'p' file
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.1 is only an alphabet table (long vowels aa ee ii oo uu shown); sec. 3.1 p. 14 notes 2sg/3sg verb forms differ by high vs low tone on the tense prefix nóo-. No stress, accent, penult or length rule. downloaded from Internet Archive copy of lidemo.net (capture 2019-07-11; and, capture 2017-08-07).

sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. 2003. Makhuwa (P30). In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, ch. 27. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Mentions 'Emarenje' only as one of the terms Malawian speakers use for varieties of Lomwe (sec. 1); its phonology/tone sections concern Makhuwa dialects (moraic structure, H-tone placement), with no statement about Marenje stress. Used for identity only.

sources.citation: Reiman, Duane. 2002. Findings from the sociolinguistic survey of the Lolo people. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-001. 44 pp. (Glottolog also lists it as Reiman 2001)
sources.note: Nothing: sociolinguistic survey with Marenje ('Marenji') wordlist, lexical-similarity and intelligibility figures; no stress, tone or length remarks. downloaded from Internet Archive copy of sil.org/silesr/2002/001/capture 2003-10-29).
sources.venue: SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-001. 44 pp. (Glottolog also lists it as Reiman 2001)

sources.citation: SIL (ed. John David Iseminger; data from Oliver Kröger workshop, Ntete, Balama, Cabo Delgado 2002). 2009. Notas gramaticais sobre Emakhuwa-Imeetto. Monografias Linguísticas Moçambicanas 6. Nampula: SIL Moçambique. 1st electronic edn 2010, 48 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; alphabet section p. 3 lists 'vogais prolongadas: aa, ee, ii, oo, uu; consoantes prolongadas: nn, mm'. Preface + sec. 1 state the data are Makhuwa-Imeetto of Cabo Delgado/Niassa (>800,000 speakers) = Makhuwa-Meetto mgh/makh1261, so Glottolog's assignment to mare1260 is wrong. downloaded from Internet Archive copy of lidemo.net (capture 2017-05-16).

sources.citation: Centre for Language Studies, University of Malawi. 2009/2010. Language Mapping Survey for the Southern Region of Malawi (Lomwe varieties incl. Marenje).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Sociolinguistic mapping of Lomwe varieties in Malawi where 'Emarenje' is a self-designation; may clarify whether Malawian Marenje is covered by any Lomwe phonology, but no stress statement expected.

sources.citation: Ibraimo, Hermínio, M. Chotama, João Osumani Pequenino, Jeffery Shrum & Margaret Shrum. 1998. Levantamento linguístico na Zambézia Ocidental em Moçambique: um levantamento sociolinguístico das populações Manyawa, Takwane, Marenje, Kokola e Lolo. Maputo: SIL. 38 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other Marenje-specific primary document listed by Glottolog; a survey, so a stress statement is unlikely, but its wordlist transcription might mark penultimate length.
